Column types, casts, factors, times of day, and conversion to model data.

## Column types

### `->cast()` {#cast}

```php
$table->cast(array $types): DataFrame
```

Convert columns to other types.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$types` | <code>array&lt;string, Type&#124;string&gt;</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `Type::parse()` {#type-parse}

```php
Type::parse(Type|string $type): Type
```

A Type from a case or its name, such as 'float' or 'date', in any letter case.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$type` | <code>Type&#124;string</code> |  |  |

**Static method** of `Phibble\Type`\
**Returns** `Type`\
**Throws** `InvalidArgumentException`: for an unknown type name.

### `Type->abbreviation()` {#type-abbreviation}

```php
$type->abbreviation(): string
```

The short label printed in a column header, as in tibble: dbl, int, lgl, chr, fct, date, dttm, time, or list.

**Method** of `Phibble\Type`\
**Returns** `string`

### `Type->isNumeric()` {#type-isnumeric}

```php
$type->isNumeric(): bool
```

Whether the type is numeric: float, int, or bool.

**Method** of `Phibble\Type`\
**Returns** `bool`

## Factors

### `->asFactor()` {#asfactor}

```php
$table->asFactor(
    string $name,
    ?array $levels = null,
    bool $ordered = false,
): DataFrame
```

Turn a column into a factor, as R's `factor()`. Without levels, they are the sorted unique values. Values not in `$levels` become NA.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |
| `$levels` | <code>list&lt;string&#124;int&#124;float&gt;&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> |  |
| `$ordered` | <code>bool</code> | <code>false</code> |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd), [Getting started](../getting-started.qmd)

### `->asOrdered()` {#asordered}

```php
$table->asOrdered(string $name, ?array $levels = null): DataFrame
```

Convert a column to an ordered factor, as R's `factor(ordered = TRUE)`.

An existing factor keeps its levels unless `$levels` is given.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |
| `$levels` | <code>list&lt;string&#124;int&#124;float&gt;&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> | Levels in order; null takes the sorted distinct values. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `DataFrame`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `->isOrdered()` {#isordered}

```php
$table->isOrdered(string $name): bool
```

Whether the column is an ordered factor.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `bool`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `->levels()` {#levels}

```php
$table->levels(string $name): array
```

The levels of a factor column, in level order.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |

## Times of day

```php

```

A time from hours, minutes, and seconds, as `hms::hms()`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$hours` | <code>int</code> |  |  |
| `$minutes` | <code>int</code> | <code>0</code> |  |
| `$seconds` | <code>int&#124;float</code> | <code>0</code> |  |

**Static method** of `Phibble\Time`\
**Returns** `Time`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `Time::fromSeconds()` {#time-fromseconds}

```php
Time::fromSeconds(int|float $seconds): Time
```

A time from a number of seconds, rounded to the microsecond.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$seconds` | <code>int&#124;float</code> |  |  |

**Static method** of `Phibble\Time`\
**Returns** `Time`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `Time::parse()` {#time-parse}

```php
Time::parse(string $text): ?Time
```

Text such as "07:30", "7:30:15.25", "-01:00:00", "100:00:00", or "1:30 PM" as a time, or null when it is not one. Unlike reading CSV, which follows readr, fractional seconds are kept.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$text` | <code>string</code> |  |  |

**Static method** of `Phibble\Time`\
**Returns** `?Time`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `Time::meridiem()` {#time-meridiem}

```php
Time::meridiem(int $hours, string $suffix): int
```

readr's AM/PM rule: 12 AM is hour 0, and PM adds 12 hours to any hour but 12.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$hours` | <code>int</code> |  |  |
| `$suffix` | <code>string</code> |  |  |

**Static method** of `Phibble\Time`\
**Returns** `int`

## Model data

### `->toModelData()` {#tomodeldata}

```php
$table->toModelData(?array $names = null): array
```

Columns for model fitting with formulas (`Phit\fit_ols`, `Phit\fit_generalized_linear`, `Phit\model_matrix`):

- float, int: list<float\|int\|null>
- bool: list<bool\|null> (a two-level contrast, as in R)
- string: list<string\|null> (the model sorts levels, as R does)
- date: days since 1970-01-01; datetime: seconds since epoch
- factor: ['levels' => list<string>, 'codes' => list<?int>, 'ordered' => bool],
  with 0-based codes, null for NA, and every level in table order

List-columns cannot be modelled and throw.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | <code>list&lt;string&gt;&#124;null</code> | <code>null</code> | Columns to include; all by default. |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `array<string, list<mixed>|array{levels: list<string>, codes: list<?int>, ordered: bool}>`\
**Examples** [Types](../types.qmd)

### `->toMatrix()` {#tomatrix}

```php
$table->toMatrix(array $names): array
```

Rows of numeric columns as floats, the shape phit's fit_* functions take for x. Bool columns become 0.0/1.0; NA stays null.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$names` | <code>list&lt;string&gt;</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `list<list<float|null>>`

### `->toVector()` {#tovector}

```php
$table->toVector(string $name): array
```

A numeric column as floats, the shape phit's fit_* functions take for y.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$name` | <code>string</code> |  |  |

**Method** of `DataFrame`\
**Returns** `list<float|null>`
